historical_commentary.text: This note shows how to create and call Oracle PL/SQL functions and stored procedures from 4D via the low-level 4D for OCI plug-in, using a recursive factorial function and a simple user/date/time-reading procedure as teaching examples. The plug-in-level OCI binding technique is Oracle- and 4D-for-OCI-specific and now legacy, but the underlying pattern of calling stored PL/SQL routines with bound input/output parameters remains conceptually identical in any Oracle integration written today, just typically via more modern connectivity layers rather than 4D for OCI.
related_updates: 4D for OCI was 4D's low-level Oracle connectivity plug-in for 4D 2004-era databases, following the discontinuation of the older, higher-level 4D Oracle plug-in
4D's later native SQL engine (v11, 2007) and evolving external database connectivity options changed how 4D applications typically integrate with SQL databases
